rule: GOAL: Move the falling block into the yellow slot using the horizontal paddle. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows slide the paddle; spacebar releases the block. RULE: The block rests on the paddle and moves with it until released. TRAP: Thinking the paddle deflects the block like a pinball bumper; it only carries it.

GOAL: Guide the snake head along the dotted path to the finish line using minimal clicks. CONTROLS: Clicking a dot ahead moves the head there, consuming space behind it. RULE: The head can only jump up to three steps forward; longer clicks fail. TRAP: Assuming you can jump further than three steps wastes actions on failed attempts.

GOAL: Reach the exit in sixteen moves. CONTROLS: Arrows move two spaces, not one. RULE: You must land on white tiles, skipping over gray ones. TRAP: Believing you can stop on gray tiles wastes turns and breaks the path.

GOAL: Move the plug down five cells to reach the socket. CONTROLS: Click marker bars and stems to set direction codes, then click the central blob to execute movement. RULE: Black bar and black stem together signal the plug to move downward. TRAP: Assuming marker position dictates direction wastes time; only the specific color combination matters for movement.

GOAL: Clear the level by clicking the top blue button three times to push the bottom wall right, filling the white area with gray. CONTROLS: Clicking the top blue button shifts the bottom gray wall rightward, expanding the gray region. RULE: The level is solved when the bottom-right white space is completely covered by the expanding gray panel. TRAP: Believing the blue block blocks the wall; the gray panel successfully overwrites or absorbs the blue block to reach the edge.

GOAL: Shrink the key tip to slide left past the bar's notch. CONTROLS: Arrows move the key; clicks toggle keypad cells to alter the tip. RULE: Matching the keypad's diamond pattern cuts the tip height to fit the gap. TRAP: Moving left fails until the tip is short enough to clear the lower bar section.

GOAL: Move the key tip up to meet the handle. CONTROLS: Arrows guide the tip; clicks set the target pattern. RULE: Matching the yellow shape triggers the key’s next movement. TRAP: Thinking the pattern size dictates the shift distance, rather than the shape acting as a simple trigger for a fixed step.

GOAL: Push sliding bars until their red dots align with the plus markers. CONTROLS: Clicking one side of a panel pushes the bar toward the opposite side. RULE: The bar extends only if the tip is adjacent to the target, not overlapping it. TRAP: Assuming pluses are static walls; they can be pushed further if enough force is applied.

GOAL: Align the piston’s yellow markers directly beneath the bar’s yellow markers. CONTROLS: Clicking the top panel moves the upper wall left; clicking the bottom panel moves the lower wall right. RULE: The mechanism stops when the internal limit is reached, requiring alternating clicks to bypass the block. TRAP: Believing you could move one wall continuously until aligned; the internal counter blocked further movement in one direction.

GOAL: Align each column's pink glyph to match its blue partner's rotation. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cursor; pressing up or down cycled the current column's pink glyph through its rotation states. RULE: The pink glyph must match the blue glyph's identity and rotation angle exactly for the column to lock. TRAP: Assuming all columns shared the same rotation cycle; column three's cycle did not contain the required pose, forcing a different alignment strategy.

GOAL: Move three boxes to slots using a cap that flips on vertical moves. CONTROLS: Arrows move and flip cap; Space attaches or detaches box in cap direction. RULE: Only attach/detach when box aligns with cap (up/down), not side. TRAP: Assuming side attaches work; they fail, forcing inefficient repositioning.

GOAL: Reach 16 units in column one, 18 in four, and 10 in five, leaving two and three empty. CONTROLS: Click left or right arrows between columns to shift white blocks two units sideways. RULE: Blocks only move if the destination column has empty space; you must build up source columns before draining them. TRAP: Ignoring that intermediate columns need temporary storage; trying to drain directly fails if neighbors lack space to receive blocks first.

GOAL: Align the tip with the marked socket. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the tip; clicking triggered the pulse. RULE: Split axis determines pulse direction; vertical split sends horizontal pulse. TRAP: Assuming pulse follows movement direction; it actually follows the split axis.

ESTABLISHED: Red grabs on right extension; green does not when head is at center 32-33. FAILED: Extending arm right while head is at center 32-33 failed to grab green. GOAL IS NOT: Simply aligning the arm with green’s band while the chain is broken. CONTROLS: UP moves head and column up 6; LEFT/RIGHT extend/retract arm; grab requires fresh right extension.

GOAL: Extend colored bars to reach specific targets by adjusting their lengths. CONTROLS: Click panel holes to shrink or grow the corresponding bar's length. RULE: Left holes shrink the bar, while right holes grow it, pushing subsequent bars away. TRAP: Assuming all bars grow in the same direction; orientation varies, so check each panel's specific mapping.

GOAL: Align seven slots so each glyph’s identity matches the codebook sequence, ignoring rotation or flip. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between slots; pressing UP cycles the glyph in the current slot. RULE: Only the glyph’s underlying identity matters; any dihedral transformation of the correct glyph counts as valid. TRAP: Assuming the glyph must match the exact orientation in the codebook wastes time on unnecessary rotations.

GOAL: Move the large piece to merge with the target. CONTROLS: Click a spot to move the piece toward it. RULE: Pieces move a limited Euclidean distance per click. TRAP: Assuming diagonal moves count as two separate steps wastes actions.

GOAL: Decode the yellow row's hidden message to fill the blue slots correctly. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate glyphs to match the required symbol identity. RULE: Only the symbol type matters, not its orientation; a rotated glyph counts as correct. TRAP: Wasting moves trying to align rotation angles perfectly, when the identity alone satisfies the check.

GOAL: Arrange four colored blocks to match the target sequence shown at the top of the screen. CONTROLS: Click a colored block in the bottom tray to select it, then click an empty slot in the middle panel to place it. RULE: Blocks must be placed in left-to-right order to match the specific color sequence displayed above the slots. TRAP: Believing you could drag blocks directly or place them out of order wastes time; you must select then place one by one.

GOAL: Position both crosses so their arms cover all matching colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected cross; Space switches selection. RULE: A cross’s center aligns with the shared row and column of its dots. TRAP: Moving crosses in the wrong order causes unnecessary path overlaps.

GOAL: Rotate the ring until the yellow block sits beneath the yellow bracket. CONTROLS: Click the left arrow to rotate counter-clockwise; the right arrow rotates clockwise. RULE: Clicking blocks does nothing; only arrow clicks move the ring and count toward your limit. TRAP: Wasting actions clicking on blocks or assuming the top dashes track remaining moves instead of just being decoration.

GOAL: Position the arm's head over the target ring. CONTROLS: Click anywhere to rotate and extend the arm toward that spot. RULE: The arm's base stays fixed; only the head moves relative to the pivot. TRAP: Believing the base moves when clicking far away wastes time; the base never shifts.

GOAL: Reduce the board to a single remaining peg. CONTROLS: Tap a peg to select it, then tap the landing spot to jump. RULE: You must jump directly over an adjacent peg into an empty space. TRAP: Assuming you can jump without an adjacent peg blocks your progress.

GOAL: Align the bottom glyph with the top icon to unlock the docked state. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the piece; landing on the pad rotates the bottom glyph. RULE: Matching pixel patterns between the two panels signals progress, not victory. TRAP: Assuming glyph alignment ends the level wastes time; it merely opens a path.

GOAL: Match the bottom-right grid to the static center pattern. CONTROLS: Click tiles to toggle red or blue. RULE: The center widget displays the fixed target pattern; it never changes. TRAP: Assuming the center widget reflects your current moves rather than the solution.

GOAL: Align two yellow blocks onto bracket targets by rotating intersecting loops. CONTROLS: Red buttons shift loop contents clockwise; green buttons shift them counter-clockwise. RULE: Shared cells update simultaneously based on the active loop’s direction during a single shift. TRAP: Assuming moves are independent; rotating one loop unexpectedly alters the other’s shared positions.

GOAL: Cover all matching colored dots with their specific shapes to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; the spacebar cycles through available shapes. RULE: Shapes must be placed so their arms or centers precisely align with the target dots. TRAP: Assuming shapes can overlap freely; incorrect layering or partial coverage leaves dots uncovered.

GOAL: Paint the grid to match the hidden target pattern shown by the widgets. CONTROLS: Click a block to toggle its color between blue and orange. RULE: The white tiles on each widget reveal the exact orange positions for their respective grid sections. TRAP: Assuming the center orange dot is just decoration; it actually defines the paint color you must use.

GOAL: Slide three shapes to cover all marked dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space cycles the selection. RULE: A shape is solved only when its center aligns with a dot. TRAP: Moving the wrong shape wastes turns; always confirm the active shape before moving.

GOAL: Turn the all-red grid orange where widgets show white. CONTROLS: Clicking grid cells changes their color; clicking widget edges rotates the widget pattern. RULE: Widgets define the target orange cells; rotate them until no white areas overlap. TRAP: Assuming widgets were static caused repeated invalid clicks; you must rotate them to resolve conflicts.

GOAL: Move the yellow block to the left target and the orange block to the right target. CONTROLS: Left and right buttons rotate their respective rings of blocks by one step. RULE: Blocks in the overlapping cells move based on which ring you choose to rotate. TRAP: Thinking you must align every block; only the yellow and orange positions matter.

GOAL: Place specific colors into numbered slots to match hidden targets. CONTROLS: Click tiles to swap positions; press space to submit your arrangement for checking. RULE: The slot order follows a diagonal path across the grid, but ignores any empty gaps. TRAP: Assuming every tile counts toward the sequence wastes turns; you must mentally skip blank spaces when counting positions.

GOAL: Move the blue block to the exit by clearing the plug blocking the path. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; SPACE marks a checkpoint, saving the current position and state. RULE: Pressing SPACE creates a ghost that replays your previous moves from the checkpoint while you control the block from the start. TRAP: Believing the ghost moves independently; it actually replays your past actions, so you must time your new moves to coincide with the ghost clearing the plug.

GOAL: Place seven colored tiles into the target row to match the sequence R, N, p, Y, M, b, O. CONTROLS: Click palette tiles to select, click panel slots to place, and press Space to confirm the level. RULE: Fill slots in left-to-right order, inserting the full green and blue panels between the red slots they interrupt. TRAP: Assuming all red slots are filled consecutively; ignoring the panels causes misalignment and wasted moves.

GOAL: Paint specific grid cells red or orange to satisfy hidden color constraints. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell cycles its color blue to red to orange back to blue. RULE: Some cells forbid orange, forcing them to stay blue or red, simplifying the target. TRAP: Assuming every cell needs a specific final color wastes clicks on unconstrained cells.

ESTABLISHED: The blue squares merge when adjacent; pressing SPACE while merged does nothing. FAILED: Merging the squares and pressing SPACE did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply bringing the two blue squares together. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blue squares independently until they touch and merge.

GOAL: Arrange seven colored pieces to match a specific target sequence. CONTROLS: Click a piece in the palette, then click a slot on the panel grid to place it. RULE: Inserting a spacer piece shifts subsequent slots, aligning pre-placed items with the target order. TRAP: Assuming slots are fixed positions rather than dynamic slots that shift when a spacer is added.

GOAL: Move the heavy block into the target ring by positioning your head relative to fixed anchors. CONTROLS: Clicking an anchor moves your head; moving your head shifts the block to the calculated midpoint. RULE: The block always sits exactly halfway between your head and the active anchor. TRAP: Assuming you can push the block directly; you must pull it by moving your head away from the anchor.

GOAL: Move the yellow block to the yellow bracket and the orange block to the orange bracket. CONTROLS: Click green arrows to move blocks right or up; click red arrows to move them left or down. RULE: Blocks slide in a straight line until they hit a wall or another block, never stopping mid-path. TRAP: Assuming a single click moves a block only one step wastes actions; long slides are efficient.

GOAL: Recolor two shapes to match their target boxes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; space switches between the X and the plus. RULE: A shape changes color only when its exact center lands on a matching colored box. TRAP: Assuming any part of the shape touching the box works; you must align the center precisely.

GOAL: Merge the two light-blue squares into one solid block. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active square; pressing an arrow twice moves the next square in the sequence. RULE: Squares combine when they occupy adjacent cells, forming a single unified shape. TRAP: Assuming both squares move simultaneously; they operate independently, requiring sequential commands to align them.

GOAL: Guide two yellow blocks to the two bracket slots at the top corners. CONTROLS: Top arrows rotate only the top row; middle arrows rotate the entire main loop. RULE: The top row is part of the main loop, so use main rotations to lift blocks up, then top rotations to align them. TRAP: Assuming top arrows affect the whole board wastes moves; they only shift the five top cells.

ESTABLISHED: Two rooms with a central wall, rings, and two movable tokens. Docking a token to a ring does not open the wall. FAILED: Clicking the wall, pressing RIGHT while docked, and moving tokens to grid edges produced no state changes. GOAL IS NOT: Simply docking tokens to rings or clicking the wall to open it. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected token; clicks select tokens or interact with objects.

GOAL: Reach the panel after rotating the logo to the target angle and collecting both yellow items. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character; landing on plus pads rotates the logo ninety degrees. RULE: Refill bars appear only on specific pads, forcing a path that collects items before running out of energy. TRAP: Assuming you can move twenty-one steps after a refill causes a game over; stop at twenty to stay safe.

GOAL: Place the block onto the target ring by moving two separate diamond anchors. CONTROLS: Click a diamond to make it the active head; click a black floor spot to move the block. RULE: The block centers itself exactly between the two diamonds after each move. TRAP: Assuming you can move both diamonds simultaneously; you must switch heads and move them one at a time.

GOAL: Align the plug with the socket and insert it to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug one step at a time in any direction. RULE: Red tips must perfectly overlap red tabs; white body parts cannot touch other shapes. TRAP: Believing you must move horizontally first; vertical alignment is crucial before approaching the socket.

GOAL: Guide two sliding tokens into their matching rings. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected token one step; clicking selects a token. RULE: Tokens slide until blocked, but push through walls to exit on the other side. TRAP: Thinking the pushed token stops at the wall; it actually slides completely through it.

GOAL: Guide the charcoal shape to the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move both shapes; horizontal inputs mirror, vertical inputs sync. RULE: Right moves charcoal right and black left; down moves both down. TRAP: Assuming shapes move independently wastes moves; every horizontal input shifts the partner opposite.

GOAL: Reach the exit by using the recording mechanic to navigate around obstacles. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character; Spacebar records and replays your previous movements as a ghost. RULE: The ghost replays your exact previous path, allowing you to trigger switches or block paths from a distance. TRAP: Thinking the ghost only plays the last segment; it actually replays all recorded moves cumulatively, requiring precise timing.

GOAL: Match the board to the hidden checkerboard pattern while satisfying dial clues. CONTROLS: Click stamps to flip plus-shaped areas; click plain cells to toggle individual colors. RULE: Dial hints indicated acceptable colors, but only the strict checkerboard parity determined the final win condition. TRAP: Assuming dial hints alone defined correctness wasted time; ignoring the underlying parity grid caused repeated failures.

GOAL: Decode the bottom blue strip by matching glyphs to the codebook. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor to select and verify glyph positions. RULE: Glyphs align with a strict seven-column pitch starting from the strip's left edge. TRAP: Assuming glyphs begin one column after the strip's start caused extraction errors.

GOAL: Move three arms to fill specific target blocks. CONTROLS: Click a diamond to make it the active head, then click a spot to move it. RULE: A block forms between the current head and the next diamond in the chain. TRAP: Assuming all arms can move simultaneously; you must finish one arm's path before starting another.

GOAL: Align the plain charcoal shape with the yellow target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows move the dotted object; SPACE switches which object is dotted and active. RULE: The wall moves three times faster than the shapes when dotted. TRAP: Assuming SPACE cycles all objects; it only toggles between the wall and the shapes.

GOAL: Guide the block to the yellow target using limited moves. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the block; clicks toggle the red bar between horizontal and vertical. RULE: The block can only stand on solid platforms; it cannot walk through air or walls. TRAP: Assuming the red bar is a permanent wall. It is a movable bridge; toggle it to cross gaps.

GOAL: Move three yellow tokens into specific marked slots. CONTROLS: Arrows rotated tokens around their star or shifted them outward along a spoke. RULE: Each star had independent controls, but one central arrow shifted all tokens along a shared outer ring. TRAP: Assuming the central ring arrow only affected one star, wasting moves trying to isolate its effect.

GOAL: Fill the grid with the correct diagonal color pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the stamp angle; clicks pick ink colors; space applies the stamp. RULE: The stamp paints a triangle where row plus column is greater than or equal to nine. TRAP: I wrongly assumed the painted area mirrored the other diagonal, wasting time on the wrong half.

GOAL: Dock the green and blue plugs into the yellow object to complete all connections. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide pieces; clicks select plugs for re-docking. RULE: Pieces must align tabs precisely; intermediate paths must remain clear during movement. TRAP: Moving the green first breaks blue connections; plan simultaneous docking or re-dock immediately.

GOAL: Paint the top triangle purple and the bottom-right triangle orange, leaving the bottom-left white. CONTROLS: Space stamps the selected shape; arrow keys rotate it; clicks select the ink color. RULE: Stamp the purple top first, then overlay the orange diagonal shape to fix the boundary. TRAP: Believing you needed a white stamp to clear errors, when simple layering suffices.

GOAL: Move two yellow blocks to specific target spots using limited moves. CONTROLS: Green shifts rows and a separate track forward; red reverses them; arrows rotate a column. RULE: Moving a block into the shared corner lets you park it, breaking the lock between row and track. TRAP: Assuming row and track always move together; ignoring the corner overlap makes the puzzle seem impossible.

ESTABLISHED: One block destruction clears a seven-row vertical column, piercing the black band. FAILED: Trying to navigate around the solid black rows without clearing the central blocks. GOAL IS NOT: A simple horizontal path; the band requires vertical destruction to pass. CONTROLS: Targeting a block removes it and the black rows immediately above and below it.

GOAL: Guide the token from the start to cover the yellow core on the gray goal box. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the token two steps per press across the grid. RULE: Stepping on the lever rotates the red barrier, opening a path to the goal area. TRAP: Assuming the barrier remains open after leaving the lever; verify the path holds before committing to the route.

GOAL: Align the wall and two shapes onto their yellow target outlines. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; mouse clicks select it; space locks it. RULE: Objects only move when white dots appear on them; clicking turns dots white. TRAP: Assuming locked shapes block the wall’s path, when they actually allow it to pass through freely.

GOAL: Arrange pieces and two rings to match a nine-slot color sequence. CONTROLS: Click pieces to place them; press space to confirm the solution. RULE: Rings inserted into the red panel replace slots with the blue panel’s contents, expanding the total length to nine. TRAP: Assuming rings act as simple placeholders; they actually duplicate the blue panel’s pattern, changing the required sequence length.

GOAL: Arrange colored panels to match a target sequence by determining their correct order. CONTROLS: Click rings to place them in the red panel to set sequence order; click pieces to fill specific panel slots. RULE: A ring’s color dictates which panel it controls, and its horizontal position determines where that panel’s three items appear in the final line. TRAP: Assuming ring color only highlights a panel without realizing its position strictly controls the insertion order, leading to misplaced groups.

GOAL: Place red, blue, and green shapes to cover all matching colored dots without overlap. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape three cells; Spacebar cycles through the red, blue, and green shapes. RULE: Each shape’s geometry must align perfectly to cover its specific color dots while ignoring others. TRAP: Assuming shapes can move one cell per press wastes actions; they always jump three cells.

GOAL: Clear the path to guide the fish to the target. CONTROLS: Clicks destroyed blocks; arrows moved the fish horizontally. RULE: The fish rises automatically only when positioned directly over an open channel. TRAP: Believing the fish rises anywhere; it must align perfectly with the gap to ascend.

GOAL: Fit rings into colored panels by nesting items to complete three slots. CONTROLS: Click palette pieces to drag them into panel slots; press space to submit. RULE: Rings can hold other pieces, allowing nested arrangements that satisfy specific color constraints. TRAP: Assuming rings are solid blockers; they are actually containers that accept inner pieces.

GOAL: Fill the canvas with specific colors by stamping geometric shapes at correct angles. CONTROLS: Click palette to select ink; arrows rotate the stamp; spacebar applies the stamp to the canvas. RULE: Only the visible handle determines the stamp's position and orientation on the grid. TRAP: Assuming the stamp rotates around its center instead of the handle's pivot point causes misaligned placements.

GOAL: Align shapes to form a specific pattern above a reflection line. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space switches between shapes. RULE: Shapes must match their mirrored reflections exactly across the active wall line. TRAP: Assuming shapes cannot pass through each other or the reflection zone during movement.

GOAL: Place three diamond shapes so their combined center coordinates match a target grid block, ensuring no shapes overlap. CONTROLS: Click a shape to select it as active; click a valid empty cell to move the active shape’s center there. RULE: Shapes are diamond-shaped (Manhattan distance), meaning diagonal neighbors are empty, not occupied. TRAP: Assuming shapes are square blocks leads to false overlap detection and invalid moves on diagonal gaps.

GOAL: Merge scattered fragments into a single shape and deliver it to the matching circle. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move a piece toward that spot, limited by a short range per action. RULE: Pieces automatically merge into a larger form when their centers fall within a tight distance threshold. TRAP: Believing you can drag a piece across the board in one click; long distances require multiple short steps.

GOAL: Reach the goal by crossing an isolated cluster using linked portals. CONTROLS: Arrows move the token; clicks activate buttons and levers. RULE: Stepping on a linked pink core and pressing its button teleports you to the paired core. TRAP: Assuming buttons only rotate bars; here, standing on a core changes the button’s effect to teleportation.

GOAL: Destroy the enemy core and reach the exit handle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the ship; mouse clicks fire the laser. RULE: Laser beams pierce through weak barriers but bounce off metal rings. TRAP: Believing the handle opens automatically; you must physically enter the glowing zone to finish.

GOAL: Move three colored blocks into a specific docked arrangement to complete the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the currently selected block; mouse clicks select a block by clicking its body. RULE: Only the block under the cursor moves, so click to switch targets before every directional input. TRAP: Assuming blocks move as a single group wastes turns; each color must be moved and positioned individually.

GOAL: Merge scattered pieces into one shape and deliver it to the target circle. CONTROLS: Clicking near a piece moves it toward the cursor within a fixed distance limit. RULE: Pieces only merge if they land adjacent to each other after a move. TRAP: Clicking a spot reachable by multiple pieces causes a no-op instead of a split or ambiguous move.

GOAL: Paint the canvas by stamping four distinct colors onto specific geometric regions defined by diagonal boundaries. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the stamp’s angle; clicking a palette selects a color; the spacebar applies the current stamp to the canvas. RULE: Each color must be applied at its unique correct angle to match the target pattern, requiring precise navigation between palette selection and rotation. TRAP: Assuming colors can be applied in any order ignores strict dependency constraints, causing wasted rotations and failed stamps when prerequisites are unmet.

GOAL: Position the shape inside the yellow zone by aligning it with the walls. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; clicking selects the next target. RULE: The shape reflects across the walls, so adjust wall positions before moving the shape. TRAP: Moving the shape first wastes actions; adjust the horizontal wall before activating the vertical one.

GOAL: Fill the grid with colored triangles and a final diagonal stripe. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the stamp orientation; Space applies the selected color. RULE: Stamps cover specific triangular regions defined by their angle, requiring precise rotation to match target zones. TRAP: Assuming all rotations are adjacent steps wastes time; some key presses jump multiple angles or cycle unexpectedly.

GOAL: Slide walls and shapes to frame the yellow figure symmetrically. CONTROLS: Arrows move selected pieces; clicks select them. RULE: Only pieces aligned with the mirror line reflect correctly. TRAP: Thinking shapes reflect automatically; you must manually align each piece.

GOAL: Move both blocks to the bottom corridor. CONTROLS: Arrows move both blocks simultaneously in that direction. RULE: Blocks stop only when hitting walls or hazards, not each other. TRAP: Believing the goal was swapping positions like Level 1; ignore prior logic and focus on descending.

GOAL: Slide the orange C piece into the top-left notch and the vertical bar into the bottom-right slot. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then use arrow keys to move it across the grid. RULE: Pieces dock only when their tabs perfectly align with the target shape’s empty slots. TRAP: Moving the C piece up before sliding it left caused a collision with the fixed U-shaped wall.

GOAL: Move the block left to the target using the machine's program. CONTROLS: Click toggles to set bar and stem colors; click the start button to execute the sequence. RULE: The black cartridge reverses execution order, reading columns right-to-left instead of left-to-right. TRAP: Assuming left-to-right execution caused you to ignore the reversed logic and waste moves on wrong toggles.

GOAL: Align two sliding shapes to match yellow target patterns on the mirrored grid. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; clicks select a shape or toggle wall visibility. RULE: The grid reflects across the center, so a shape's position mirrors symmetrically on both sides. TRAP: Believing walls block shape movement; they are visual aids only, allowing shapes to pass through freely.

GOAL: Ride the shifting bar to the exit while avoiding stranding on black walls. CONTROLS: Arrows move the token; clicks shift the bar’s position. RULE: The bar cycles through phases; moving it strands the token if it leaves no cover. TRAP: Assuming the bar moves one step per click; it actually jumps phases, causing instant failure if you misjudge the next safe column.

GOAL: Fill the bar and guide the logo to the exit panel. CONTROLS: Arrows move the piece; landing on pads rotates the logo or refills the bar. RULE: The mosaic pad permanently changes the logo’s color, which must match the exit. TRAP: Thinking pads vanish after use; they persist, so avoid redundant visits that waste moves.

ESTABLISHED: The water is trapped below a solid six-block wall. Destroying the leftmost block opens a gap, but water does not spread right until adjacent blocks are broken sequentially. FAILED: Trying to clear blocks out of order or skipping the leftmost section stopped the flow. The fish stayed stuck in the lower pocket. GOAL IS NOT: Simply breaking the wall anywhere. Random destruction does not connect the path. CONTROLS: Click blocks to destroy them. The fish swims toward open water spaces.

GOAL: Guide four blocks into their matching colored rings without getting stuck. CONTROLS: Click a block to select it, then use arrow keys to move it one step. RULE: Only the selected block moves; pushing another block does not change which one is active. TRAP: Assuming the pushed block becomes selected wasted moves sending the wrong piece away from its target.

GOAL: Clear the board by merging remaining pegs into a single unit. CONTROLS: Click pegs to jump over neighbors; click plugs to slide them along wires. RULE: Pegs can jump directly onto plug cells, riding the plug to new locations. TRAP: Assuming plugs are static obstacles; they actually serve as mobile bridges to reposition pegs.

GOAL: Rotate six plug columns to set their internal wire colors, then slide the final plug into its matching socket. CONTROLS: Click a column's top to cycle its color state; click the side stem to toggle specific wire connections. RULE: The socket only accepts a plug if its slot color matches the column's background and its wires align with the target pattern. TRAP: Assuming all columns share the same color logic; each column's slot color independently dictates which wire state is valid.

ESTABLISHED: The paddle deflects the rising block upward. Static red bars block the left and center paths. The right path leads to the ceiling. FAILED: Deflecting the block left or center hits red bars. Deflecting right hits the ceiling. All three cup slots were attempted. GOAL IS NOT: Entering any of the three visible cups. The win condition is not reaching the top row. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the paddle horizontally. Space launches the block. R resets the level.

ESTABLISHED: Yellow socket retracts when blue and ghost occupy same tile; stays out if only one present. FAILED: Single block coverage; ghost arriving at different time than freeze. GOAL IS NOT: Simply parking ghosts at their specific assigned sockets without considering final position overlap. CONTROLS: Movement steps create ghost paths; final position determines freeze state; socket reacts to current tile occupancy.

GOAL: Slide the plus shape right to dock it in the square ring, then move your green token into that ring. CONTROLS: Arrows move your green token. Walking into a plus pushes it one step in that direction. RULE: You can only push a plus if the space behind it is completely empty. TRAP: Believing your token advances after a push. It stays put, so plan extra moves to reposition before the next push.

ESTABLISHED: The orange is unglued from the VW. The green blocks the orange's downward path. The pink overlaps the orange's upper range. FAILED: Shrinking the green to free the orange. Growing the green to push the orange up. GOAL IS NOT: Absorbing both plus signs simultaneously. CONTROLS: Growing expands cells, pushing adjacent blocks. Shrinking retracts cells. Contact drags glued blocks.

ESTABLISHED: The yellow piston is six units wide; the gate opening is three units wide. The piston currently sits in the first strip, while the target gap is in the third strip. FAILED: Attempting to push the solid six-wide piston directly through the three-wide gate opening. GOAL IS NOT: Simply sliding the intact, six-wide piston block into the distant gap without modification. CONTROLS: Arrows move the piston within its current white strip. Opening the gate removes the orange block but does not widen the passage.

GOAL: Reach the top exit by consuming the enemy blocking the path. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; walking into an enemy removes it. RULE: Enemies only kill you when they lunge; you can safely step into them. TRAP: Assuming contact with an enemy is fatal leads to wasted turns seeking a bypass.

GOAL: Navigate two pieces to their targets by pushing markers into dead ends to clear the path. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active piece; pressing a direction moves the piece and pushes any marker in that line. RULE: Markers are unpassable and block movement, but become passable floor once they are pushed into a dead-end corner. TRAP: Confusing left and right directions when navigating narrow corridors, causing failed attempts to push markers out of the way.

GOAL: Deliver a box to a target slot while a bot handles another delivery. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; SPACE attaches or releases a box. RULE: The bot automatically releases its box at the first empty slot along its path. TRAP: Assuming you can freely use all target slots; the bot claims spots based on its route, forcing you to adapt your destination.

GOAL: Clear the level by shrinking a tip, teleporting it, destroying two rings, and climbing a handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip; clicks trigger specific tools like shrinking, teleporting, or firing rays. RULE: Positioning the tip correctly before using a tool ensures the action targets the intended object. TRAP: Assuming the tip’s orientation remains constant after movement leads to misaligned tool usage.

GOAL: Guide the hero to the exit while avoiding the stationary enemy's line of sight. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the hero one tile in the chosen direction. RULE: The enemy detects you only if you are directly aligned and unobstructed. TRAP: Assuming the enemy moves; it does not, so you can safely circle around it.

ESTABLISHED: A fixed permutation moves blocks between specific cells. Yellow markers confirm three mappings. FAILED: Pressing controls does not clear the level; blocks merely shift positions according to the hidden pattern. GOAL IS NOT: To stop movement or remove blocks; the puzzle requires arranging them into a specific target configuration. CONTROLS: Pressing a button executes the global permutation once, moving every block to its assigned destination cell simultaneously.

ESTABLISHED: The game is Peg Solitaire. A jump requires a peg, an adjacent peg, and an empty landing spot. Each jump removes the middle peg. FAILED: Random moves and trying to fill the protruding edge cells first did not reduce the peg count effectively. GOAL IS NOT: Clearing the board or filling every hole; the win condition is strictly having exactly one peg remaining. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click the landing spot to jump. Each jump consumes two actions.

GOAL: Align matching glyphs in every box to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selection cursor; pressing selects and rotates the active box. RULE: A box is solved only when all glyphs inside share the same visual class. TRAP: Forgetting multi-glyph boxes require every glyph to match, not just one.

GOAL: Navigate the maze without colliding with the orange patroller. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move you; each move advances the orange one step. RULE: The orange bounces between the top and bottom walls on a fixed eight-step cycle. TRAP: Believing a wasted move stalls time; invalid inputs do not advance the orange, leaving you stuck.
